formulas.name: Coulomb's Law
formulas.expression_raw: F = kq₁q₂/r² = (1/(4πε₀))(q₁q₂/r²) — k ≈ 9×10⁹ N⋅m²/C², ε₀ = 8.85×10⁻¹² F/m
formulas.topper_tip: ⚠️ Common Trap: Always express distance 'r' in meters (not cm or mm), and ensure charges are in Coulombs (convert µC by 10⁻⁶). In a dielectric medium of constant K, F_med = F_air / K.

formulas.name: Electric Field
formulas.expression_raw: E = F/q = kQ/r² (point charge) — E in N/C. Direction: away from +ve, toward -ve charge
formulas.latex: E = F/q = kQ/r^2 (point charge) - E in N/C. Direction: away from +ve, toward -ve charge
formulas.topper_tip: ⭐ Pro Tip: Electric field due to a point charge follows the inverse-square law. Field lines never intersect because at the intersection point there would be two directions of field, which is impossible.

formulas.name: Electric Potential
formulas.expression_raw: V = kQ/r, V = W/q (work per unit charge) — V in volts (J/C). Potential energy U = qV = kQq/r
formulas.note: V = W/q (work per unit charge) — V in volts (J/C). Potential energy U = qV = kQq/r
formulas.topper_tip: ⭐ Pro Tip: Electric potential is a scalar quantity! When finding net potential at a point, calculate algebraically with sign (positive for +q, negative for -q).
